text: Every TV and radio in America just blasted the same alarm, at the exact same moment.
That was the nationwide emergency alert test, and your phone stayed quiet because phones were left out this time.
For a real national alert, only the President can give the order.
That message shoots out to about eighty special radio stations across the country.
Each one has a shelter with heavy sealed doors, built to stay on the air through hurricanes, or even a blast that kills the power grid.
Every other station is always listening, and the second they hear the alarm, they pass it on, like falling dominoes.
That loud buzzing at the very start is actually computer code, telling every machine what kind of alert is coming.
It's built so the President can reach more than nine out of ten Americans within ten minutes.
In the first big test back in 2011, lots of stations missed it, and one TV company played Lady Gaga instead.
The whole thing started after the Cuban missile crisis, so the President could warn everyone if missiles were coming.
And in over fifty years, no President has ever used it for real.
